title: Shannon intrinsic randomness from Reed-Muller hashing
summary: Prove that Reed-Muller parity-check hashing attains the Shannon intrinsic-randomness rate of every memoryless Bernoulli source.

formal_statement.body: Let $Z^n$ consist of independent $\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\delta)$ bits. For every $\delta\in(0,1)$ and every output rate $\widehat R<h(\delta)$, construct a sequence of binary Reed-Muller codes $C_n$ with parity-check matrices $H_n$ and $n^{-1}\operatorname{rank}(H_n)\to\widehat R$ such that $D(P_{H_nZ^n}\|P_{U_{\operatorname{rank}(H_n)}})\to0$. Equivalently, prove that the associated nested Reed-Muller construction achieves the strong-secrecy capacity of the binary wiretap channel.

scope.domain: Deterministic randomness extraction and strong-secrecy wiretap coding with Reed-Muller codes
assumptions: The source is memoryless Bernoulli with fixed bias delta
The extractor is a parity-check map from a nested sequence of binary Reed-Muller codes
Uniformity is measured by KL divergence, corresponding to Renyi order one
scope.unresolved_remainder: The source proves intrinsic-randomness achievability for integer Renyi orders $p\ge2$ and a weaker $p=1$ rate condition $R>(1-2\delta)^2$. Achievability of every output rate below the Shannon entropy $h(\delta)$, equivalently strong-secrecy capacity for the nested Reed-Muller construction, remains open.

progress.summary: The source asks whether Reed-Muller parity-check maps attain Bernoulli intrinsic randomness at Renyi order one, equivalently the associated strong-secrecy capacity.
